idea-plugin.name: OAuthLint
idea-plugin.description:
OAuthLint catches OAuth, OIDC, JWT, MCP, session, cookie, and CORS anti-patterns that AI coding tools frequently produce, and surfaces them as native inline annotations while you edit. This includes a dedicated MCP server-auth pack (token pass-through, RFC 8707 audience binding, unauthenticated transports, tool-handler SSRF) for the TypeScript and Python MCP SDKs.

It scans the current file on open and on save and highlights each finding with a gutter marker and a tooltip that carries the rule id, the explanation, and a link to the rule documentation. Where a fix is available you can apply it with an Alt+Enter quick fix, or suppress the finding with an inline comment. A "Scan Project" action runs one pass over the whole project and lists every finding in a tool window with click-to-navigate. Severity is mapped to the IDE's own error, warning, and weak-warning levels.

OAuthLint is fully self-contained. The rule pack ships inside the plugin and a small pinned scan engine is downloaded once and verified against a pinned SHA-256 checksum. There is nothing else to install.

Supported languages: ten in all, from JavaScript and Python to Go, C#, and Kotlin, activated automatically wherever the matching language support is present. The 270+ rule pack adds framework-aware coverage (ASP.NET Core, Gin/Echo/Fiber, Hono + better-auth, FastAPI, Ktor, Laravel/Socialite, Rails/Devise/OmniAuth/Doorkeeper) alongside the MCP server-auth pack.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.0

  • Apply fixes from the editor. Findings that carry a suggested fix now offer an Alt+Enter quick fix that rewrites the code in place. Two more intentions were added on every finding: suppress it with an inline comment, and open its rule documentation.
  • Scan the whole project. A new "OAuthLint: Scan Project" action (Tools menu) runs one pass over the entire project and lists every finding in a dedicated OAuthLint tool window at the bottom, with double-click navigation to the exact line. Previously findings appeared only in files you had open.
  • Branded gutter icon. Lines with a finding now show the OAuthLint mark in the gutter.
  • The bundled rule pack was refreshed and its cache key bumped so it stays current on upgrade.

0.4.1

  • Compatibility with 2025.x IDEs. The plugin now loads in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, and the other IDEs from 2024.2 onward, including the 2025.1, 2025.2, and 2025.3 releases (earlier builds capped the supported range at 2024.3, which hid the plugin from newer IDEs in Marketplace search). Checked with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier. No rule changes.

0.4.0

  • Mobile auth: Swift/iOS and Android. 18 new rules for the auth mistakes AI assistants ship in mobile apps: tokens in UserDefaults or SharedPreferences instead of the Keychain/keystore, cleartext traffic, OAuth in embedded WebViews, hardcoded secrets, and more. Covers Swift (iOS, Vapor) and Android (Kotlin plus manifest and config XML).
  • 270+ rules total; inline diagnostics now cover Swift and Android XML too. The extraction cache key was bumped so the new rules load on upgrade.

0.3.0

  • New languages: PHP, Ruby, and Kotlin. The pack now spans ten languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#/.NET, PHP, Ruby, and Kotlin), with framework-aware rules for Laravel/Socialite (PHP), Rails/Devise/OmniAuth/Doorkeeper (Ruby), and Ktor (Kotlin).
  • More framework packs. ASP.NET Core (C#), Gin/Echo/Fiber (Go), Hono + better-auth (TS), and FastAPI (Python).
  • 250+ rules total; the extraction cache key was bumped so the new rules load on upgrade.

0.2.1

  • MCP server-auth coverage. Catches the OAuth 2.1 mistakes Model Context Protocol servers ship: token pass-through (confused deputy), missing RFC 8707 audience binding, unauthenticated transports, and tool-handler SSRF, for the official TypeScript and Python MCP SDKs.
  • Rule pack refreshed; the extraction cache key was bumped so the new rules load on upgrade.

Full release notes: github.com/Auspeo/oauthlint/releases
